full_judgment:
A.T.M. Afzal, J: This appeal by leave is from order dated 10 August, 1986 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division (at Jessore) in Criminal Misc. Case No. 39 of 1986 refusing to grant bail to the appellant, an accused, along with others, in Dumuria P.S. Case No. 4 dated 10.5.86 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 22 of 1986 which was under investigation. 

 3. One police constable who was on duty along with others at the polling centre lodged an F.I.R. with Dumria P.S. on the following day i.e. 8th May in connection with the said occurrence and named aforesaid deceased Harun and one Abdur Rouf as accused along with many others who were said to be involved in the occurrence. This FIR gave rise to Dumuria P.S. Case No. 3 dated 8.5.86 under various sections of the penal Code corresponding to G.R. Case No. 21 of 1986. On 10.5.86 another FIR giving a different version of the occurrence was lodged with Dumuria P.S. by aforesaid Abdur Rouf (accused in the first FIR). There the present appellant was named as accused No. 1 in a list of 36 accused and the fact of death of Harun at the Sadar Hospital was disclosed. This gave rise to Dumuria P.S. Case No. 4 dated 10.5.86 under various sections of the Penal Code including section 302 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 22 of 1986 as already stated. 

 5. It appears that the learned Judges of the High Court Division refused to grand bail as it was felt that the petitioner (appellant) should be kept in custody till investigation of the case is concluded for the sake of fair and proper investigation in the case". This feeling was generated because of a statement made in the affidavit-in-opposition filed on behalf of the State to the effect that "since the petitioner (appellant) is the Chairman of the Union and an influential man of the locality, there is every chance of tampering with evidence if he remain on bail." 

 7. Being satisfied, prima facie, that there was substance in the contention of the appellant, we allowed ad-interim bail to him while granting leave on 10 September, 1986. His bail was not confirmed by the High Court Division, because, as has been noticed above, the case was under investigation. Whether the High Court Division was justified in refusing bail in the facts of the case need not be considered any more as we are informed by the parties that the investigation is over, the charge-sheet has been submitted and the case is pending trial in the Sessions Court. The Sessions Judge will now consider the question of bail of the appellant upon appearance of the appellant in that court. Until then he will remain on bail already granted by us.
